corrections.source_says: met: the abstract explicitly compares realized videos with creators’ prior videos along semantic and topical dimensions and compares output across creators. These are outcomes assessed on produced output, although the scoring methods and numerical diversity estimates are unavailable. This correction does not establish random assignment or core eligibility.
corrections.quote: Consistent, treated creators’ videos become more similar to their own prior output along semantic and topical dimensions, reducing within-creator diversity; however, their output does not become more similar to other creators’ output.
corrections.locator: Crossref API abstract for DOI 10.2139/ssrn.6910898 (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2139%2Fssrn.6910898), sentence beginning "Consistent, treated creators".

corrections.source_says: Company involvement is unreported in the accessible abstract, which identifies YouTube as the study setting but contains no funding, acknowledgments, or company-involvement disclosure. A confirmed false is unsupported; record null/unknown and explain that disclosures could not be checked.
corrections.quote: Our setting is YouTube’s rollout of the Inspiration Tab, an ideation feature that suggests video ideas, hooks, and storylines but does not generate videos.
corrections.locator: Crossref API abstract for DOI 10.2139/ssrn.6910898 (https://api.crossref.org/works/10.2139%2Fssrn.6910898), complete abstract and sentence beginning "Our setting is"; no disclosure section was available.

confirmed: The form’s source.version correctly identifies an abstract-only Crossref reading of a 2026 SSRN working paper; Crossref metadata confirms the recorded title and author spellings (Crossref API record for DOI 10.2139/ssrn.6910898, title, author, posted, subtype, and group-title fields).

No markdown or PDF is on file: retrieval.json marks c604 not_obtained. The complete Crossref and Semantic Scholar abstracts and the Mannheim repository record were read; SSRN and the repository-linked ResearchGate page returned HTTP 403, and Mannheim marks full_text_status as none (retrieval.json, c604; https://madoc.bib.uni-mannheim.de/72493/, metadata and Abstract).

The reported study is a matched panel of incumbent YouTube creators analyzed with difference-in-differences using U.S.-European regional access variation, supporting design_class observational and context_class observational. No randomized-people study is described; has_randomized_people_study=false means none identified in the accessible abstracts, not that inaccessible full-text studies have been ruled out (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Exploiting regional variation").

Null randomized and analyzed participant counts, arm counts, and output counts are appropriate: none is reported. The 50-person threshold and whether fewer than 50 people were analyzed cannot be checked; 4.1% is a production effect, not a participant count (Crossref abstract, complete abstract).

The Inspiration Tab supplies video ideas, hooks, and storylines and does not generate videos; the abstract does not name its underlying model or establish individual use (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Our setting is").

S1-O1 reported and the one-line finding reproduce the production effect exactly: "Access increases video production by 4.1%." No interval, standard error, or p-value accompanies it (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Access increases video production" and complete abstract).

S1-O2 reported correctly states greater semantic and topical similarity to the same creator’s prior output, hence lower within-creator variety; coding this as flexibility rather than across-person diversity follows the codebook. The abstract gives no numerical diversity estimate or uncertainty (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Consistent, treated creators"; creativity-codebook.md, section 6).

S1-O3 reported correctly states that output does not become more similar to other creators’ output; no numerical effect or uncertainty is supplied, so the one-line finding should not imply a demonstrated zero effect (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Consistent, treated creators", clause beginning "however").

All three reported strings and the one-line finding match the Crossref abstract. Core inclusion is not established, and this is an empirical observational study rather than a synthesis; the empty pooled-estimate fields are appropriate (Crossref abstract, methods and results sentences).
summary: The accessible abstract supports observational context and the reported 4.1% production increase, reduced within-creator diversity, and no increase in similarity across creators; no randomized-people study is identified. The output-scored eligibility criterion should be met and company involvement is unreported, while participant counts and full-text methods remain unverified.
